title: Turn-based JRPG game template. What would you add?
author: Gaebabi
selftext:
Here’s a quick look at a turn-based JRPG game template I’ve been building in Unity with a React-based UI. It includes character upgrades, inventory, summons, combat, and settings.

I used Codex with Astra at max reasoning to help develop the C# logic, and a Unity-React UI framework asset from the Asset Store for the UI. I used Codex imagegen for the artwork. Most of my time has gone into polishing transitions, reusable components, and character animation.

The characters and backgrounds are placed in the Unity world, separate from the UI, so you can swap them out for your own 3D models and environments.

Any features you’d add or improve? Anything that feels unnecessary, overly AI-generated, or worth removing?

Still a work in progress, so don’t hold back with the feedback. I’d appreciate your honest feedback.

comments.author: marsb3a
comments.body:
Good: Visually very beautiful, i love how the characters look and UI looks polished.

Bad: No gameplay. Clicking "confirm attack" is not fun. No unique mechanics or anything. Shards, fragments, credits, passes etc. Looks like you built a fully decked out cash shop but forgot to develop the game.

replies.author: count023
replies.body: look to the Persona series and Expedition 33's menus, displays and interactions to see how they make their turn based games feel \_alive\_ and involved, right now yours looks nice but plays flat like a gameboy era pokemon game. The best TBS games tehse days make even menu interactions feel like part of the action. Camera close ups on characters, changing poses when they're desicding what action or activities to do, that kind of thing.

replies.author: Gaebabi
replies.body: Thank you, I was looking for works to reference, and these are great examples.
